key_insight: QCCDCert uses one Lean-verified compiler to explore QCCD hardware designs while proving that compiled programs preserve behavior and obey each design’s hardware rules.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can compare trapped-ion layouts, trap sizes, and operating constraints with formally verified compilation rather than trusting separate compiler implementations.
method: Supply hardware descriptions and operating rules as compiler inputs.
Use a single correctness theorem covering all supported candidate designs.
Guide an AI agent’s device proposals with compiler-checked results.
evidence_signal: Across 75 benchmarks with 11–130 qubits, the best evaluated design averaged 66% less modeled execution time than the worst equal-capacity design; AI-proposed devices beat the fastest evaluated design on 71 benchmarks.
watch_item: Reported speedups are based on modeled execution time, so physical-device gains depend on how faithfully the hardware rules and timing models capture real operation.
paper_title: QCCDCert: Formally Verified Compilation for QCCD Co-Design
